judge_assessment.explanation: Every value the judge says it recomputed is correct: 2(96+60+40) = 392 sq cm; a 6.5 by 3.25 cm room at 1 cm = 4 m is 26 m by 13 m with perimeter 78 m; 2 pi (3)(3+8) = 66 pi = 207.35 sq cm; the grid polygon encloses 52 sq m; the shed's four walls plus roof are 60 + 24 = 84 sq m; a 5 by 3 cm deck scales to 20 by 12 = 240 sq m; the label is (8 pi + 1)(11) = 287.46 sq cm; two L-panels are 2(40+18) = 116 sq m; 148 x 5^2 = 3700 sq cm; 128 + 32h = 448 gives h = 10 cm; and the tank scales to r = 2 m, h = 8 m so 32 pi + 4 pi = 113.10 sq m. The judge's manual review of problem 11 is exact - the cube's surface area is 216 sq cm against the flat box's 252 sq cm at equal volume, so Box A uses less cardboard - and the key does avoid double-counting joined faces. I also confirmed the two figures against their stems: the problem 4 grid polygon is a 3 by 4 block on an 8 by 5 block, giving 52, matching the declared vertices, and the problem 8 L-panel is drawn to the stated 10-by-4-plus-6-by-3 proportions. The finding the judge missed is curriculum labelling: eight of the twelve problems - including both cylinder surface-area items - are tagged '3.MD.C.7 / 3.MD.D.8', a Grade 3 area-and-perimeter pairing, and the answer key prints '3.MD.C.7 / 3.MD.D.8 - problems 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11' directly under 'Level: Grade 6-7 - Geometry'. The task contract names 6.G / 7.G and references/standards-map.md carries the row 'Area, surface area, volume (gr 6-7) | 6.G.A / 7.G.B'.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 11 is the best handling of a mixed open item in this shard: it is declared as a manual verify entry whose description carries the two surface areas (216 and 252) so the open item still pins its numbers, and the key supplies a model answer plus explicit grading latitude ('Award credit for any well-argued practical reason (shipping, shelf display, product shape, ease of packing) that is stated alongside the correct numerical comparison').

Problem 12's synthesis genuinely chains three ideas that could each be done alone: scale the drawing to real dimensions, halve the diameter to a radius, then paint the curved wall and the top but not the base - with the declared trap (painting both circles, 125.66) naming the likeliest slip.

The scale-factor items are sequenced to expose the length-versus-area distinction directly: problem 2 scales lengths (perimeter 78 m), problem 6 scales an area with the stem's warning 'the scale factor for lengths is not the scale factor for areas' (240 sq m), and problem 9 applies 5^2 rather than 5 to a surface area (3700 sq cm).
Problem 5 removes the floor from the painted area and problem 1 keeps all six faces, so the student has to read what the object needs rather than apply one prism formula everywhere.

root_causes.description: scripts/verify.py documents 'standard' as a reporting tag that never gates, while scripts/render_quick_answers.curriculum_block prints those same tags verbatim on the answer key beneath the grade level. Nothing checks a tag against the sheet's band, so an off-grade code chosen during generation reaches the reader unchallenged - the exact failure references/standards-map.md warns about in its own preamble.
evidence: evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-195/verify.json: problems 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10 and 11 declare "standard": "3.MD.C.7 / 3.MD.D.8", including the two cylinder surface-area items (7.G.B territory)
evals/runs/curriculum-shardX-20260802T194403Z/tasks/curr-195/answer_key.pdf page 1 prints 'Level: Grade 6-7 - Geometry' then '3.MD.C.7 / 3.MD.D.8 - problems 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11'
references/standards-map.md carries the correct row 'Area, surface area, volume (gr 6-7) | 6.G.A / 7.G.B' and warns in its preamble against borrowing a lower-grade domain
The packet's task contract declares standard_refs '6.G / 7.G'

improvements.title: Gate the printed CCSS tags against the sheet's declared grade band
improvements.proposed_change: verify.py documents 'standard' as a reporting tag that never gates, while render_quick_answers.curriculum_block prints those same tags verbatim on the answer key directly beneath the grade level. Add a gate that reads the leading grade of each declared code and fails when a tag sits more than one grade below the sheet's declared band, naming the correct row from references/standards-map.md in the failure message. Restate in the standards map that the fix for a missing topic is to add the row with the real code, never to borrow the nearest lower-grade domain.
improvements.regression_test: Add a gate test using curr-195's verify.json: a Grade 6-7 geometry sheet whose cylinder surface-area problems declare '3.MD.C.7 / 3.MD.D.8'. The gate must exit non-zero and quote the 6.G.A / 7.G.B row; retagging to 7.G.B.4 and 7.G.B.6 must exit 0. No gate reads the tag today, so the first assertion fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The Curriculum block stops telling a parent or teacher that a Grade 4-5 or Grade 6-7 packet covers a Grade 2 or Grade 3 standard, which is the one place on the packet an adult looks to place the work in a curriculum.
improvements.risk: Deliberate below-band review content would trip the gate, so allow an explicit per-problem acknowledgement that a prior-grade standard is intended.

case_summary: An excellent multistep geometry-and-scale packet. All eleven machine results and the manual design comparison recompute correctly, both figures match their stems and their declared vertices, units are printed on every answer line, the interleave forces method choice, and problem 11 shows the right way to declare an open item - manual, with the checkable numbers carried in the description and explicit grading latitude in the key. The one defect is the printed curriculum claim: eight of twelve problems, including cylinder surface area, are tagged with a Grade 3 area-and-perimeter pairing and the answer key prints it beneath 'Level: Grade 6-7'. Only the adult-facing metadata is wrong; the mathematics and the pedagogy are not.
